lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Label the profile link as LinkedIn rather than leaving it as a bare URL.
items.because: That makes its purpose obvious.

items.says: Consider adding relevant coursework, focus areas, or academic distinctions.
items.because: Include them only if they strengthen your fit for the roles you want.

items.says: Check that the MBA degree status and dates are accurate and consistent with the rest of your materials.
items.because: The dates indicate the MBA is complete.

items.says: Make your intended direction clear alongside the mechanic role.
items.because: It follows an MBA and analytical and product-related work.

items.says: Clarify how many jobs the under-five-day dry-dock measure covers.
items.because: That makes the performance claim easier to assess.

items.says: Say whether under five days is typical, a target, or an improvement over a prior baseline.
items.because: That makes the performance claim easier to assess.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to inspection readiness or the scale of the work.
items.because: The bullet describes responsibilities but not the result.

items.says: Place the Harbor Payments internship above Crestline.
items.because: Experience entries should be in reverse-chronological order.

items.says: Clarify what decisions or changes the scorecards and review meeting drove.
items.because: This is the least outcome-oriented bullet in the role.

items.says: Clarify whether the 30% reduction is relative or a percentage-point change.
State the period over which the pick-error change was measured.
Define S&OP on first use.
items.because: Some readers may not know the abbreviation.

items.says: Clarify how forecast error was measured.
items.because: The methodology may not be self-evident.

items.says: Separate or prioritize the rollout, procedure changes, training, and negotiations.
items.because: Combining them obscures your role and the source of the 1,800-hour saving.

items.says: Clarify whether the driver-hour savings were measured or projected.
Explain what the single verification step means.
Clarify which part of the onboarding redesign you personally owned.
State that the conversion change is five percentage points, not a five-percent relative increase.
Clarify the rollout scope meant by all merchants.
items.because: It may not mean the entire company.

items.says: Explain what prioritization decision resulted.
items.because: The bullet reads more like a method note than an accomplishment.

items.says: Clarify how you adapted or applied Reach in RICE.
items.because: Readers may question using support tickets as its measure.

items.says: Make the result and its relationship to the research and business case clear.
items.because: The list of activities is long, but the result is unclear.

items.says: The roadmap-prioritization outcome overlaps with the previous bullet.
items.because: The same outcome should not be repeated across both bullets.

items.says: The testing and conversion result repeat the earlier checkout bullet.
items.because: Both bullets should be kept only if they show distinct contributions.

items.says: Clarify the A/B test's unit of analysis.
Explain what reporting the effect on customers means.
items.because: The measured outcome is checkout conversion.

items.says: Clarify how the two-region rollout relates to the earlier pilot region.
Check whether the rollout result repeats the onboarding bullet.
Consider whether the Campus Food Rescue App should be more prominent than less relevant experience.
items.because: The project may be more relevant to your target role.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 means eligible students, registered users, or actual users.
Specify how the nine-tonne figure was measured.
Check that in its first year aligns with the project dates.
The stated 150% increase does not match the user counts.
items.because: An increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%.

items.says: Support the claim that reminders caused the user increase.
items.because: Interviews can inform a feature choice but do not by themselves establish causation.

items.says: The fill-rate change is misstated as 20%.
items.because: A rise from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% relative increase.

items.says: Clarify how the fill rates across the two dining halls were aggregated.
Distinguish the estimated saving from a realized saving.
Make the saving model's assumptions or scope clear.
items.because: Readers need to understand what was modeled.

items.says: The client-funded pilot overlaps with the approval in the final practicum bullet.
items.because: The same milestone should not be reported twice.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to mapping intake and shortening the form.
items.because: The passive construction obscures your role.

items.says: Show the size or operational result of shortening the form, if available.
items.because: The bullet does not show the effect of the change.

items.says: The pilot approval appears to repeat the funding decision in the first practicum bullet.
items.because: The same milestone should not be reported twice.

items.says: Make sure the listed skills reflect work you can discuss in detail, particularly A/B testing and roadmapping.
Consider whether the tools list reflects those required by your target roles.
items.because: Add other tools only if you have genuine working proficiency.
